Metadata.title: Dominik Huber | Full-Stack Developer
Metadata.description: Full-stack developer with a focus on UI/UX design, born in Ulm and at home in Cologne. I build fast, thoughtful web apps with Next.js, React and TypeScript.

HomePage.bio:
Hi, I'm Dominik, a full-stack developer with a focus on UI/UX design. I was born in Ulm, and today I'm at home in Cologne. I studied automotive and engine engineering, but somewhere between design and software engineering I found my real passion.

It all started in the sneaker scene. With JavaScript, HTML and CSS I built my first tools, which later helped more than 1,000 users buy limited releases. Small scripts turned into real products, and the question “How do I automate this?” more and more often became “How do I build this better?”

After that, I dug deeper into backend systems, APIs and scalable software, and eventually built ProfitPath together with fellow founders: my first big SaaS, made with <next>Next.js</next>, <react>React</react>, <ts>TypeScript</ts>, <go>Go</go> and <postgres>PostgreSQL</postgres>. Today, thousands of users rely on ProfitPath for access to more than 200 million product records, updated daily.
HomePage.bioAfterGraph: I'm especially drawn to thoughtful interfaces, micro-interactions and the small details you don't consciously notice, but without which a design never feels quite right. I design with an engineer's understanding and build with a designer's eye.

story.p1: I probably spend more time in front of a screen than I'd like to admit. But at least it's usually for a good reason. I love writing code, turning new ideas into something real and building, step by step, a thought into something that actually works in the end. Most of the time, anyway.
story.p2: My interest in technology goes far beyond programming, though, especially when it comes to <apple>Apple</apple>. Since the iPhone 4, I've followed every new product with a mix of excitement and the question of whether I really need it. The answer is sitting in my living room: an entire sideboard full of Apple boxes. Throw them away? Unthinkable. They're well designed too.
story.p3: When I need a break from the screen, you'll often find me on the <golf>golf course</golf>. I like the mix of calm, focus and the fact that this sport regularly reminds you not to take yourself too seriously. Some days everything goes exactly as planned, and on others you're just happy to find your ball again. To clear my head on the other days, I also go running and hit the gym regularly. There, at least, you always know where the weight is. Except in some McFit gyms, where word apparently hasn't spread yet that you put the weights back after your workout.
story.p4: And then there's <latam>Latin America</latam>. My first trip to Colombia, together with one of my business partners, left a lasting mark on me and changed what I think of as wealth. I met people there who couldn't be more open and warm, and who take every chance to share their lives and their culture with you. At the same time, many of them face problems every day that are hard to imagine from here, some just to get by. Since then, I see it this way: rich isn't whoever writes the biggest numbers. Rich is being healthy, having a roof over your head and being able to walk to the fridge without a worry to make yourself something to eat.

TechStackPage.title: Tech stack
TechStackPage.description: The tools and technologies Dominik Huber works with: Next.js, React, TypeScript and more.
TechStackPage.intro: The tools I work with and the projects they're part of. It all started with JavaScript and CSS, without any types. Today I build applications that are type-safe end to end, from frontend to backend: from sign-in and payments to databases handling millions of reads and writes. These aren't all the tools I use, but they're the essential ones.

nextjs.name: Next.js
nextjs.description: App Router with React Server Components: whatever the server can render stays on the server. Cache Components and Partial Prerendering serve a static shell from the cache and stream the rest into it. ProfitPath and this site run on it, here with every page prerendered per language.

react.name: React
react.description: Components, hooks and a renderer that schedules updates by priority: transitions keep the interface responsive while work happens in the background, and Suspense handles loading states. The interfaces of ProfitPath and this site are built with it.

reactNative.name: React Native & Expo
reactNative.description: React components that render real native views, through the New Architecture with Fabric and TurboModules. Expo Router, EAS Build and over-the-air updates take care of navigation, builds and releases. That's how the NexosSolutions and ProfitGo apps for iOS and Android each came out of a single codebase.

chromeExtensions.name: Chrome extensions & Webpack
chromeExtensions.description: Built on Manifest V3: a service worker instead of a persistent background page, content scripts in an isolated world on the page and a strict Content Security Policy. Webpack bundles popup, service worker and content scripts from multiple entry points. Browser extensions were the core of NexosSolutions, and ProfitGo is available as a Chrome extension too.

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.description: Structural typing, control-flow inference and generics make the interfaces between frontend, API and database checkable before any code runs. Strict mode is the default in ProfitPath and on this site.

javascript.name: JavaScript
javascript.description: Single-threaded with an event loop, plus promises and async/await for everything that waits on the network. NexosSolutions was a browser extension in plain JavaScript that automated selecting, buying and checking out limited items through web requests.

python.name: Python
python.description: Concise syntax and a huge ecosystem for data. For a university in Munich, I used it to build a project that collects data from the web for research and teaching: requests and tls-client for requests that identify like a real browser, BeautifulSoup to parse HTML and pandas for the analysis.

go.name: Go
go.description: Goroutines and channels for concurrency without managing threads, compiled into a single static binary. At ProfitPath, a Go backend delivers the data to the frontend and answers the API requests.

nodejs.name: Node.js & Express
nodejs.description: JavaScript on the server: an event loop with non-blocking I/O, built for many concurrent requests. With Express as the middleware pipeline, it ran the API behind NexosSolutions that fed the extension and the app with data.

orpc.name: oRPC
orpc.description: Procedures instead of endpoints: the client calls them like local functions, and types and schema validation apply on both sides, without any code generation. If needed, the same router is served as a REST API with an OpenAPI spec. At ProfitPath, oRPC connects frontend and backend, together with TanStack Query.

tanstack.name: TanStack
tanstack.description: Query caches server data per key and refreshes it in the background, stale-while-revalidate. Table is a headless engine for sorting, filtering and pagination, leaving the look entirely to your own code. At ProfitPath they power the large product tables; on this site, the commit calendar arrives in the browser prerendered through Query.

postgresql.name: PostgreSQL
postgresql.description: Relational, with MVCC so reads and writes run in parallel without blocking each other, and indexes like B-tree and GIN, including for JSONB. At ProfitPath, PostgreSQL serves more than 200 million products, updated daily.

mongodb.name: MongoDB
mongodb.description: Documents instead of tables: flexible schemas in BSON and an aggregation pipeline for multi-stage analysis. At NexosSolutions, it held the user and product data of the extension and the app, and NexosProxies stored its data in MongoDB as well.

supabase.name: Supabase
supabase.description: A full PostgreSQL with auth, Row Level Security right in the database, Realtime, Edge Functions and Storage. At ProfitPath we use it far beyond the database: RLS, database triggers and functions, Edge Functions and Storage, plus syncing subscriptions.

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.description: Checkout and Billing for payments and subscriptions, signed webhooks for everything that happens asynchronously, and idempotency keys so a retried request never charges twice. At ProfitPath, Stripe handles payments with flexible payment options.

betterAuth.name: Better Auth
betterAuth.description: Authentication as a self-hosted TypeScript library: your own database through adapters, plugins for two-factor, passkeys and organizations with roles. Now in use at ProfitPath as well.

profitpath.title: ProfitPath
profitpath.description: A platform for Amazon sellers. Finds profitable products for online arbitrage: more than 200 million products, updated daily and served from PostgreSQL, plus CSV scanning, competitor analysis, automatic profit calculation and much more.

profitgo.title: ProfitGo
profitgo.description: For retail arbitrage. The second product in the ProfitPath family: product analysis, automatic profit calculation, returns handling, product tracking and much more.

nexossolutions.title: NexosSolutions
nexossolutions.description: Automated checkout software. A browser extension and a mobile app built with Expo and React Native that make buying limited releases easier: release automation, bot protection bypasses and much more.

nexosproxies.title: NexosProxies
nexosproxies.description: Proxy networks. My own dedicated residential and datacenter proxies over IPv4 and IPv6, SOCKS5 proxies, Squid as the proxy server, authentication in the IP:PORT:USER:PASSWORD format and much more.

portfolio.title: huberdominik.com
portfolio.description: My portfolio, the site you're on right now: bilingual, with streaming text, static and partial prerendering, server-side rendering, data fetching with TanStack Query and much more.

CvPage.title: Curriculum Vitae
CvPage.description: CV of Dominik Huber, full-stack developer: roles, projects and experience.
CvPage.intro: My CV, read like a git log: the latest commit on top, the initial commit from 1997 at the very bottom. In between, a branch switch from automotive and engine technology to software, a few companies founded as forks of their own and today the main branch ProfitPath. Running since 1997 and far from finished. At first, I thought I'd find my path in the automotive industry. Somewhere along the way, I found it in web development instead, and that's where I've been at home ever since.
